question_text: Aerial lifts are driven or repositioned only in their lowered boom state.
recommendation: Lower boom assemblies fully prior to moving or repositioning mobile aerial work platforms.

question_text: Portable power tools are maintained in safe condition with intact casings.
recommendation: Remove damaged, cracked, or malfunctioning power tools from jobsite service.

question_text: Machine and saw guards are securely attached and fully functional.
recommendation: Reinstall manufacturer blade and belt guards; prohibit operating tools without operational guards.

question_text: Circular saw blade guards are free-acting and not wedged or pinned back.
recommendation: Release wedged lower saw guards immediately and prohibit pinning guards back during operation.

question_text: Pneumatic and hydraulic hose connections are secured with safety pins or whips.
recommendation: Install whip checks and safety locking pins across all pressurized hose couplings.

question_text: Airless spray guns have operational trigger locks and tip safety devices.
recommendation: Install manufacturer nozzle guards and verify trigger lockouts engage properly on spray guns.

question_text: Powder-actuated tools are stored unloaded in locked cases when not in use.
recommendation: Lock powder-actuated tools and powder loads inside secure cases accessible only to licensed operators.

question_text: Powder-actuated tool operators possess valid qualification cards on site.
recommendation: Verify and retain physical proof of powder-actuated tool training cards for all operators.

question_text: Working clearance in front of electrical switchgear and panels is maintained.
recommendation: Maintain at least 36 inches of clear, unobstructed access in front of all electrical panels.

question_text: Electrical panels and switchboxes are labeled with voltage and disconnects.
recommendation: Apply legible circuit and voltage warning labels on all temporary and permanent breaker panels.

question_text: Temporary circuits and 120V tool receptacles are protected by GFCIs.
recommendation: Install and test ground fault circuit interrupters on all temporary power outlets and generator leads.

question_text: Extension cords are continuous, unfrayed, and free of splices or taps.
recommendation: Discard spliced, damaged, or taped flexible cords and replace them with continuous heavy-duty cords.

question_text: Temporary lighting strings have protective cages over bulbs.
recommendation: Install protective wire lamp cages over all temporary string lighting bulbs to prevent breakage.

question_text: Power cords and temporary wiring are kept out of standing water.
recommendation: Elevate electrical cords and junction boxes above damp ground and standing water pools.

question_text: Portable generators are properly grounded or utilize verified floating neutral.
recommendation: Bond generator frames or install earth ground rods per manufacturer guidelines before energizing loads.

question_text: Lockout and tagout hardware is applied to de-energized circuits under work.
recommendation: Lock and tag open circuit breakers or disconnects before allowing work on exposed electrical systems.

question_text: Fire extinguishers are inspected monthly, tagged, and fully charged.
recommendation: Inspect fire extinguishers monthly, update service tags, and recharge any units with low pressure.

question_text: Fire extinguishers are clearly marked and unobstructed throughout the site.
recommendation: Post high-visibility signage and maintain 3 feet of clear access to all portable fire extinguishers.

question_text: Flammable liquids are stored in UL-listed metal safety cans with spark arrestors.
recommendation: Replace non-compliant plastic containers with approved metal safety cans equipped with flame arrestors.

question_text: Compressed gas cylinders are chained upright with protective valve caps on.
recommendation: Secure compressed gas bottles upright with steel chains and thread valve caps tight when not in use.

question_text: Oxygen and fuel gas cylinders in storage are separated by 20 feet or a 5-foot wall.
recommendation: Separate oxygen cylinders from fuel gases by 20 feet or a 5-foot fire-rated noncombustible barrier.

question_text: Hot work areas are shielded with fire-retardant screens and cleared of combustibles.
recommendation: Erect noncombustible welding screens and remove combustible materials within 35 feet of hot work.

question_text: Torches have operational flashback arrestors and backflow check valves.
recommendation: Install reverse-flow check valves and flashback arrestors on both torch regulators and hoses.

question_text: Safety Data Sheets are accessible to employees on every shift.
recommendation: Keep Safety Data Sheets for every hazardous chemical where employees can reach them without asking a supervisor.

question_text: All secondary chemical containers are labelled with contents and hazards.
recommendation: Label every secondary container with the product name and hazard information before it leaves the storage area.

question_text: Cal/OSHA DOSH permit is posted for excavations 5 feet deep or deeper.
recommendation: Obtain and post a Cal/OSHA activity permit prior to beginning excavations 5 feet or deeper.

question_text: Excavations 5 feet or deeper have engineered shoring, shielding, or benching.
recommendation: Install trench shields, hydraulic shoring, or slope soil back to the approved angle of repose.

question_text: Competent person conducts daily pre-shift inspections of trench walls and soil.
recommendation: Have the designated competent person inspect trenches and protective systems daily before crew entry.

question_text: Trench egress ladders or ramps are located within 25 feet of lateral travel.
recommendation: Place access ladders or ramps in trenches 4 feet or deeper so lateral travel does not exceed 25 feet.

question_text: Spoils, tools, and heavy equipment are set back from excavation edges.
recommendation: Store excavated spoil piles, materials, and mobile equipment at least 2 feet back from trench lips.

question_text: Walkways crossing over excavations have standard guardrails installed.
recommendation: Install sturdy crossover walkways equipped with standard 42-inch top rails, midrails, and toeboards.

question_text: Advance warning signs, channelizing cones, and barricades protect traffic zones.
recommendation: Set up advance warning signs, cones, and high-visibility channelizers according to the traffic control plan.

question_text: Dedicated flaggers are certified and equipped with stop/slow paddles.
recommendation: Deploy certified flaggers wearing high-visibility apparel and utilize illuminated or rigid stop/slow paddles.

question_text: Slings, chains, shackles, and rigging hardware are labeled and defect-free.
recommendation: Remove worn, kinking, or unrated slings from service and tag verified working load limits on all hardware.

question_text: Hoisting hooks have functional safety latches installed across throat openings.
recommendation: Repair or replace damaged hook safety latches to prevent accidental disengagement of rigging slings.

question_text: Crane and hoist rigging operations are directed by a qualified rigger.
recommendation: Ensure only documented qualified riggers rig loads and attach hoisting lines.

question_text: Forklift operators have valid training certification cards available on site.
recommendation: Verify all powered industrial truck operators hold current Cal/OSHA training certification cards.

question_text: Forklift pre-shift mechanical inspection checklists are completed daily.
recommendation: Complete and record daily pre-shift forklift safety checklists before operating machines.

question_text: Forklift forks are lowered flat on the ground when parked.
recommendation: Lower forklift forks completely flush to the deck and set parking brakes whenever unattended.

question_text: Heavy manual bagged materials are restricted in weight or lifted mechanically.
recommendation: Provide mechanical lifting aids or require two-person team lifts for manual handling exceeding 50 lbs.

question_text: Protruding vertical rebar is capped with approved impact-resistant covers.
recommendation: Cap all exposed vertical rebar ends with steel-reinforced mushroom caps or wooden trough covers.

question_text: Concrete cutting and grinding tools utilize active wet suppression or vacuum dust collection.
recommendation: Connect continuous wet suppression hoses or HEPA vacuum shrouds to all masonry saws and grinders.

question_text: Masonry walls over 8 feet high are braced against overturning collapse.
recommendation: Install structural diagonal bracing on newly laid masonry walls exceeding 8 feet until cured and tied.

question_text: Limited Access Zones are marked and barricaded during masonry wall erection.
recommendation: Establish and barricade a Limited Access Zone equal to wall height plus 4 feet on the non-scaffold side.

question_text: Structural steel members are secured with two bolts per connection prior to release.
recommendation: Secure solid web steel beams with at least two wrenched bolts per connection before releasing hoist lines.

question_text: Tilt-up wall erection and brace plans engineered by a licensed engineer are on site.
recommendation: Maintain the registered engineer's certified tilt-up erection and bracing plan at the jobsite trailer.

question_text: Tilt-up lifting hardware possesses a 5-to-1 safety factor against working loads.
recommendation: Verify all lifting inserts and rigging components maintain an engineered 5:1 working load safety factor.

question_text: The written Injury and Illness Prevention Program is implemented and up to date.
recommendation: Update and fully implement the written Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) to reflect current workplace operations.

question_text: IIPP safety responsibilities are clearly defined for all personnel.
recommendation: Document and communicate designated safety roles and responsibilities to all employees and supervisors.

question_text: Ongoing safety training is delivered at the frequency the IIPP requires.
recommendation: Hold safety training at the frequency stated in your IIPP and document each session.

question_text: Workplace violence prevention training is conducted for employees.
recommendation: Conduct and document workplace violence prevention training covering hazard reporting and response procedures.

question_text: New employees receive documented safety orientation before starting work.
recommendation: Deliver and document a safety orientation covering site hazards and emergency procedures before a new employee starts work.

question_text: A written Return to Work program is in place.
recommendation: Develop and document a written Return to Work policy that defines transitional modified-duty procedures.

question_text: A designated Return to Work coordinator trains supervisors on return-to-work protocols.
recommendation: Appoint a Return to Work coordinator and train supervisory staff on managing modified-duty assignments.

question_text: A written Bloodborne Pathogen exposure control plan is established.
recommendation: Establish and maintain a written Bloodborne Pathogen exposure control plan for staff with potential exposure.

question_text: A written Hazard Communication program is maintained on site.
na_label: No hazardous chemicals used on site
recommendation: Keep a written Hazard Communication program on site covering labelling, Safety Data Sheets and employee training.

question_text: A current inventory of hazardous chemicals on site is maintained.
recommendation: Compile and date a list of every hazardous chemical on site and update it whenever a product changes.

question_text: Safety Data Sheets are accessible to employees on every shift.
na_label: No hazardous chemicals used on site
recommendation: Keep Safety Data Sheets for every hazardous chemical where employees can reach them without asking a supervisor.

question_text: All secondary chemical containers are labelled with contents and hazards.
na_label: No hazardous chemicals used on site
recommendation: Label every secondary container with the product name and hazard information before it leaves the storage area.

question_text: Hazardous chemicals are stored safely according to compatibility.
na_label: No hazardous chemicals used on site
recommendation: Segregate and store chemical containers safely based on manufacturer compatibility charts.

question_text: First aid kits are accessible and unobstructed at all times.
recommendation: Relocate first aid kits so they are reachable without a key, a ladder or moving stored material.

question_text: Emergency action plan with clinic locations and phone numbers is posted.
recommendation: Post the emergency action plan detailing primary clinic locations and emergency contact numbers.

question_text: Fire extinguisher training is provided to employees annually.
recommendation: Provide and document annual hands-on fire extinguisher operation training for designated staff.

question_text: Cal/OSHA and California labor law postings are displayed in employee areas.
recommendation: Post all current mandatory Cal/OSHA and state employment posters in a visible break or muster room.

question_text: The OSHA 300A annual summary is posted February through April.
recommendation: Post the certified OSHA 300A summary in a common area from 1 February to 30 April each year.

question_text: Forklift safety rules poster is posted in powered industrial truck operating areas.
recommendation: Post Cal/OSHA operating safety rules in visible areas where forklifts or industrial trucks operate.

question_text: Required safety hazard and warning signs are mounted and visible.
recommendation: Clean, replace, or mount required safety warning and operational signs in appropriate work areas.

question_text: A certified personal protective equipment hazard assessment is documented.
recommendation: Complete and certify a written workplace hazard assessment identifying required PPE for each job task.

question_text: Required PPE is stocked and readily available for worker use.
recommendation: Replenish inventory so required PPE of proper sizing is directly available to exposed employees.

question_text: A mandatory slip-resistant footwear policy is enforced.
na_label: No slip or wet surface hazards
recommendation: Establish and enforce a written slip-resistant footwear policy for personnel working on wet floors.

question_text: Cut-resistant gloves are worn when operating cutting equipment or knives.
na_label: No commercial cutting or slicer equipment
recommendation: Require and enforce the use of cut-resistant gloves during all knife handling and slicer operation.

question_text: Employees are trained on safe operation of commercial food mixers.
na_label: No commercial food mixers on site
recommendation: Provide and document equipment-specific operator safety training before authorizing commercial mixer use.

question_text: Employees receive documented training on deli meat slicer safety.
recommendation: Conduct and document safe operating training on commercial deli slicers before permitting employee operation.

question_text: Back brace safety training is provided if back braces are supplied by the employer.
recommendation: Train workers on lifting ergonomics and the proper fitting limitations of employer-provided back braces.

question_text: Equipment-specific written lockout/tagout procedures are documented and available.
na_label: No equipment with multiple energy sources
recommendation: Draft and post equipment-specific hazardous energy control procedures for each serviceable machine.

question_text: Lockout/tagout procedures are utilized during equipment cleaning and maintenance.
recommendation: Enforce lockout/tagout protocols to isolate all energy sources prior to equipment cleaning or repair.

question_text: Documented vehicle pre-trip safety inspections are performed regularly.
recommendation: Implement and log daily documented vehicle safety inspections before placing fleet units into service.

question_text: Drivers receive regular safety training on driving hazards and defensive driving.
recommendation: Schedule and document recurring safe driving and road hazard training for all assigned drivers.

question_text: Drivers are actively enrolled in the California Employer Pull Notice program.
recommendation: Enroll all authorized commercial and company drivers in the California DMV Employer Pull Notice program.

question_text: Fall protection equipment is inspected and in good serviceable condition.
recommendation: Conduct documented inspections of all harnesses, lanyards, and hardware, removing damaged units.

question_text: Employees exposed to fall hazards are actively tied off.
na_label: No work at elevated fall exposures
recommendation: Require workers exposed to fall hazards to tie off immediately using approved personal fall arrest systems.

question_text: Personal fall arrest anchorages support required structural weight.
recommendation: Attach personal fall arrest systems only to certified anchorages capable of supporting 5,000 lbs per worker.

question_text: A written site-specific fall rescue plan is established.
recommendation: Develop and review a site-specific fall rescue plan detailing prompt retrieval of suspended workers.

question_text: Full-body harnesses and positioning devices are fitted and worn properly.
recommendation: Train and enforce proper fitting of fall protection harnesses, ensuring chest and leg straps are snug.

question_text: Free-fall distance and swing radius are calculated to prevent lower-level contact.
recommendation: Calculate total fall clearance and swing radius to ensure arresting equipment prevents lower-level impact.

question_text: Fall restraint systems are rigged to prevent workers from reaching unguarded edges.
recommendation: Adjust travel restraint lifelines and lanyards to physically prevent employees from reaching open edges.

question_text: Vertical and horizontal lifelines are free of defects and properly maintained.
recommendation: Replace frayed or damaged lifelines and verify all end terminations and tensioners meet specifications.

question_text: Employees using fall protection have completed documented training.
recommendation: Provide and document fall protection training covering harness donning, inspection, and tie-off procedures.

question_text: Employees working near unprotected sides and edges are protected from falls.
recommendation: Install standard guardrails, covers, or personal fall protection along all unprotected sides and edges.

question_text: Employees performing excavation work have received required safety training.
recommendation: Provide and document excavation safety training for all personnel entering or working near trenches.

question_text: A DOSH project permit is posted for excavations 5 feet deep or deeper.
recommendation: Obtain and post a valid Cal/OSHA (DOSH) excavation permit before breaking ground on trenches 5 feet or deeper.

question_text: A qualified competent person inspects excavations and protective systems daily.
recommendation: Ensure a designated competent person conducts and logs inspections of trenches before workers enter.

question_text: Qualified personnel perform underground utility locating before excavating.
recommendation: Have qualified personnel locate and mark all underground utilities before initiating excavation work.

question_text: Walkways over excavations are equipped with standard guardrails.
recommendation: Install standard top rails, midrails, and toeboards on all walkways or bridges crossing excavations.

question_text: Safe egress ladders or ramps are located within required lateral travel distance.
recommendation: Install ladders or ramps inside trenches 4 feet or deeper so lateral travel to an exit does not exceed 25 feet.

question_text: Trenches 5 feet or deeper are shored, benched, or protected by trench boxes.
recommendation: Install engineered trench boxes, shoring, or proper benching on all excavations 5 feet or deeper.

question_text: Employees are prohibited from working under suspended excavator loads.
recommendation: Enforce strict boundaries ensuring no personnel stand or work beneath suspended excavator buckets or loads.

question_text: Soil classification has been determined by a designated competent person.
recommendation: Have a competent person classify soil type using visual and manual tests prior to selecting protective systems.

question_text: Excavations 4 feet or deeper with hazardous atmospheres are tested before entry.
recommendation: Conduct and document atmospheric testing for oxygen, combustible gas, and toxics before entering trenches.

question_text: Secured barricades or warning signs protect open excavations from foot traffic.
recommendation: Erect physical barricades, covers, or warning signs around open excavation perimeters.

question_text: An excavation collapse emergency rescue plan is established.
recommendation: Document a trench collapse emergency plan and verify rescue equipment is accessible on site.

question_text: Trenches are backfilled promptly upon completion of subsurface work.
recommendation: Backfill open trenches promptly following work completion to eliminate ongoing cave-in and fall exposures.

question_text: Spoil piles and equipment are set back from the edge of the excavation.
recommendation: Move spoil piles, excavated material, and heavy equipment at least 2 feet back from the trench edge.

question_text: Scaffolds are erected and inspected under the supervision of a competent person.
recommendation: Ensure a designated competent person supervises scaffold erection, alteration, and daily inspections.

question_text: Safe access and egress ladders or stairs are provided to scaffold platforms.
recommendation: Install attached ladders, stair units, or direct safe access to all scaffold working platforms.

question_text: Scaffold planking is intact, scaffold grade, and fully decked across supports.
recommendation: Fully deck scaffold platforms using intact, scaffold-grade lumber or approved metal manufactured planks.

question_text: Toeboards are installed on open sides of scaffold platforms over required height.
recommendation: Install standard 4-inch toeboards on open sides and ends of scaffold platforms elevated over 7.5 feet.

question_text: Guardrails with top and midrails are securely attached to open scaffold sides.
recommendation: Install and secure compliant top rails and midrails along all open working edges of the scaffold.

question_text: Scaffolds are tied off and secured to structures at required height ratios.
recommendation: Tie off or guy the scaffold to the structure according to height-to-base ratio engineering requirements.

question_text: Scaffold base plates and mudsills are set on firm, level, and solid foundations.
recommendation: Place base plates on sound mudsills resting on level, compacted footing capable of carrying the full load.

question_text: Wheel casters on rolling Baker scaffolds are locked during work operations.
recommendation: Lock all caster wheel brakes before permitting personnel to climb or work from rolling scaffolds.

question_text: A written, site-specific Heat Illness Prevention Plan is available on site.
recommendation: Keep a written site-specific Heat Illness Prevention Plan on site covering water, shade, rest and emergency response.

question_text: Shade is erected and open to employees whenever temperatures require it.
recommendation: Erect shade at the work area and keep it open and accessible whenever the temperature trigger is reached.

question_text: Cool potable drinking water is provided in sufficient quantity for the crew.
recommendation: Supply at least one quart of cool potable water per employee per hour and refill it throughout the shift.

question_text: Shade structures are within a short walk of the working crew.
recommendation: Relocate shade structures so crews can reach them within five minutes of leaving the work area.

question_text: Required federal and Cal/OSHA workplace posters are displayed.
recommendation: Post current federal and Cal/OSHA workplace posters in a visible employee break or gathering area.

question_text: The nearest MPN clinic and hospital locations are posted with emergency numbers.
recommendation: Post the Medical Provider Network clinic and emergency hospital addresses and contact numbers clearly.

question_text: Exits, stairs, and walkways are clear of trash and debris.
recommendation: Clear all debris and obstructions from exits, walkways, and stairways immediately.

question_text: Floor drains are covered with secure grates.
recommendation: Install secure drain covers on all open floor drains to prevent tripping and fall hazards.

question_text: Hoses and nozzles transporting iodine pre-dip are free of leaks and damage.
recommendation: Replace damaged or leaking chemical hoses and dispensing nozzles.

question_text: Gates, chains, and latches operate smoothly and are in good repair.
recommendation: Repair or replace bent, broken, or improperly latching gates and hardware.

question_text: Height of circulating fans from the floor or working surface.
recommendation: Mount circulating fans at least 7 feet above the floor or install compliant safety guards.

question_text: Maximum opening dimension of protective guards on circulating fans under 7 feet.
recommendation: Install guards on fan blades with openings no larger than 0.5 inches.

question_text: Milking barn floors provide slip resistance using mats, grates, or textured finishes.
recommendation: Install anti-slip mats, clean drains, or texture slick floor surfaces to prevent slips and falls.

question_text: Milk bottle transport trailers have locking mechanisms to prevent tables flipping unexpectedly.
recommendation: Install or repair positive locking mechanisms on bottle washing transport tables.

question_text: All secondary chemical containers are labelled with contents and hazards.
recommendation: Label every secondary container with the product name and hazard information before it leaves the storage area.

question_text: A minimum 20-B:C rated fire extinguisher is mounted near fuel storage tanks.
recommendation: Mount a readily accessible fire extinguisher rated at least 20-B:C adjacent to the fuel station.

question_text: Fuel dispensing pumps are equipped with self-closing nozzles and quick shut-off valves.
recommendation: Install approved self-closing nozzles and emergency quick shut-off valves on fuel pumps.

question_text: Above-ground fuel tanks have adequate secondary containment in good condition.
recommendation: Provide certified secondary containment capable of holding fuel tank capacity per requirements.

question_text: Physical bumpers or bollards protect fuel tanks against vehicle collisions.
recommendation: Install sturdy guard posts or concrete barriers around tanks exposed to vehicular traffic.

question_text: Fuel storage areas are free of weeds, trash, and dry combustible material.
recommendation: Clear all dry weeds, brush, and combustible materials away from the fuel storage footprint.

question_text: No Smoking signs are clearly posted around fuel storage and dispensing areas.
recommendation: Post conspicuous "No Smoking" signs at fuel storage tanks and dispensing points.

question_text: Flammable materials are stored in designated cabinets with appropriate fire extinguishers nearby.
recommendation: Store flammable liquids inside approved flammable storage cabinets with an extinguisher nearby.

question_text: Chemical and oil spills are cleaned up immediately.
recommendation: Clean up chemical and oil spills immediately and dispose of waste absorbent properly.

question_text: Hand and power tools are neatly stored when not in use.
recommendation: Return hand and power tools to racks or toolboxes when not actively in use.

question_text: Extension cords and tool cables are in good condition without tape repairs.
recommendation: Remove damaged cords from service and replace them rather than using tape splices.

question_text: Compressed gas cylinders are chained upright with oxygen and fuel gases separated.
recommendation: Secure compressed gas cylinders upright and separate fuel gas from oxygen by 20 feet or a 5-foot firewall.

question_text: Oily and solvent-soaked rags are placed in self-closing metal disposal cans.
recommendation: Provide and use UL-listed metal oily rag waste cans with self-closing lids.

question_text: Grinder tool rest distance from the grinding wheel.
recommendation: Adjust the bench grinder work rest to maintain a clearance of 1/8 inch or less from the wheel.

question_text: Bench and pedestal grinders have proper wheel guards and tongue guards in place.
recommendation: Install compliant safety guards and tongue guards on all bench and pedestal grinders.

question_text: Stationary grinders and drill presses are securely bolted to the floor or bench.
recommendation: Anchor pedestal grinders, drill presses, and stationary tools securely to the floor or benchtop.

question_text: Circular saws, table saws, and power tools have intact functional safety guards.
recommendation: Ensure power saw guards retract freely and strictly prohibit pinning back guards.

question_text: Site inspection records are documented and retained.
recommendation: Document each site safety inspection with date, findings and corrective actions, and retain the records.

question_text: Abrasive wheels receive a ring test prior to installation on grinders.
recommendation: Conduct a visual inspection and tap ring test on abrasive wheels before mounting to ensure integrity.

question_text: Warning signs are posted for equipment with automatic restarting or magnetic switches.
recommendation: Post automatic-restart warning signage or install anti-restart safety switches on shop equipment.

question_text: Power take-off (PTO) shafts on tractors and implements have intact safety shields.
recommendation: Install and maintain rotating shields and master shields over all operational PTO shafts.

question_text: Trailers and towed implements are connected using safety pins rather than makeshift bolts or wire.
recommendation: Replace makeshift pins, wire, or bolts with rated safety hitch pins and locking clips.

question_text: Equipment operators wear seat belts on ROPS-equipped tractors and machinery.
recommendation: Enforce seat belt use for all operators running machinery equipped with roll-over protection.

question_text: Height of fixed ladder before a safety cage or fall arrest system is required.
recommendation: Install safety cages, rest platforms, or ladder climbing fall arrest systems on fixed ladders over 20 feet.

question_text: Hay stacks and large round bales are stable, tiered, and bound securely against collapse.
recommendation: Restack and interlock hay bales securely to prevent collapse and falling material hazards.

question_text: High-visibility reflective vests are worn by ground personnel in feed mixing and traffic areas.
recommendation: Require all ground workers around mobile feeding equipment to wear high-visibility reflective vests.

question_text: Warning signs warning of flowing grain hazards are posted on grain bins and gravity wagons.
recommendation: Post warning signs at all grain bins and wagons alerting workers to engulfment and flowing grain hazards.

question_text: Grain bins, silos, and hoppers have permit-required confined space warning signs posted.
na_label: No silos or bins on site
recommendation: Post visible "DANGER - PERMIT-REQUIRED CONFINED SPACE - DO NOT ENTER" signage at all bin access points.

question_text: Manure pits, pump sumps, and lift stations are posted as permit-required confined spaces.
recommendation: Post confined space warning signs and restrict unauthorized entry to manure pits and sumps.

question_text: First aid kits are accessible and unobstructed at all times.
recommendation: Relocate first aid kits so they are reachable without a key, a ladder or moving stored material.

question_text: Manure lagoons and open storage pits are enclosed by secure perimeter fencing.
recommendation: Install and maintain secure perimeter fencing with locked access gates around manure lagoons.

question_text: Warning and hazard warning signs are posted around lagoons and manure pits.
recommendation: Post prominent safety warning signs along manure lagoon banks and pit perimeters.

question_text: Physical stop bumpers or wheel chocks are used when backing equipment to lagoons or pits.
recommendation: Install solid stop barriers or mandate wheel chocks when backing agitator pumps and tractors to manure pits.

question_text: Manure pump drivelines and handling equipment are fully guarded.
recommendation: Guard all exposed drive shafts, chains, pulleys, and belts on manure pumps and separator equipment.

question_text: A written emergency action and evacuation plan is available on site.
recommendation: Maintain an updated written emergency action plan on site and review procedures with staff.

question_text: Emergency assembly points and evacuation maps are clearly posted.
recommendation: Post clear emergency evacuation maps and designated outdoor assembly points in employee areas.

question_text: A reliable communication system is functional to summon emergency assistance.
recommendation: Provide a functional radio, landline phone, or cellular device dedicated for emergency calls.

question_text: Fire extinguishers are inspected and tagged monthly.
recommendation: Conduct and document monthly fire extinguisher inspections on inspection maintenance tags.

question_text: Conspicuous location signs are installed above all fire extinguishers.
recommendation: Mount high-visibility identification signs directly above all fire extinguisher stations.

question_text: First aid kits are present and fully stocked for the crew size.
recommendation: Stock first aid kits to the required contents for the crew size and restock them after every use.

question_text: Walking travel time to an emergency eyewash station from a chemical hazard.
recommendation: Relocate eyewash units so they are reachable within a 10-second unobstructed walk from hazardous chemicals.

question_text: Emergency eyewash valves activate in one second or less and stay open hands-free.
recommendation: Repair eyewash valves to ensure stay-open operation without manual holding once triggered.

question_text: Eyewash stations are clean, inspected weekly, and identified by prominent signs.
recommendation: Clean eyewash bowls, install conspicuous signage, and document weekly activation flushing.

question_text: Portable eyewash solution bottles are sealed and within manufacturer expiration dates.
recommendation: Replace expired personal eyewash bottles immediately with sealed, current sterile solution.

question_text: Electrical receptacles provide functional 3-wire grounding.
recommendation: Replace ungrounded or damaged receptacles with properly grounded 3-wire outlets.

question_text: GFCI protection is installed on outlets in damp, wet, or outdoor locations.
recommendation: Install Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters on all electrical outlets located outdoors or in wet wash areas.

question_text: Overhead power lines maintain adequate vertical clearance from mobile farm equipment.
recommendation: Mark overhead lines and maintain safe clearance distances between high lines and tall equipment.

question_text: Electrical panel boxes and conduit fittings have all knockouts and filler plates closed.
recommendation: Install approved snap-in knockout seals and breaker blank plates on open panel board spaces.

question_text: Clearance maintained in front of electrical service panels.
recommendation: Maintain at least 36 inches of unobstructed clearance in front of all electrical panels and switchboards.

question_text: Separation distance between flammable or combustible storage and electrical panels.
recommendation: Relocate all flammable liquids and combustible storage at least 20 feet away from electrical panels.

question_text: Circuit breakers in all electrical distribution panels are legibly labeled.
recommendation: Label every circuit breaker switch legibly to show its designated equipment or room load.

question_text: IIPP documents night harvest safety procedures and is accessible on-site.
recommendation: Update the IIPP to document all night harvest safety procedures and maintain a copy accessible at the worksite.

question_text: Written Night Work Safety Plan is available on-site.
recommendation: Maintain an operational written Night Work Safety Plan on-site during all night operations.

question_text: A written, site-specific Heat Illness Prevention Plan is available on site.
recommendation: Keep a written site-specific Heat Illness Prevention Plan on site covering water, shade, rest and emergency response.

question_text: Ongoing safety training is delivered at the frequency the IIPP requires.
recommendation: Hold safety training at the frequency stated in your IIPP and document each session.

question_text: New employees receive documented safety orientation before starting work.
recommendation: Deliver and document a safety orientation covering site hazards and emergency procedures before a new employee starts work.

question_text: Acclimatization procedures are provided for employees adjusting to night shift work.
recommendation: Implement a structured acclimatization schedule allowing workers time to adjust to night-shift conditions.

question_text: Stop-work conditions are clearly defined and communicated.
recommendation: Define hazardous environmental and operational conditions that require immediate work stoppage and communicate them to the crew.

question_text: Specific personnel are designated with clear stop-work authority.
recommendation: Formally assign and communicate stop-work authority to designated on-site personnel.

question_text: Written emergency response plan addresses night-specific rescue and response.
recommendation: Develop and implement written emergency response procedures tailored specifically to night-shift rescue and terrain conditions.

question_text: Night-time emergency response drill has been conducted with all shift workers.
recommendation: Conduct an emergency response drill during night hours to verify employee familiarity with evacuation and response procedures.

question_text: Emergency assembly point is designated with a worker accountability procedure.
recommendation: Establish a clearly marked emergency meeting location and implement a rapid head-count accountability procedure.

question_text: System accounts for all workers before, during, and after the work shift.
recommendation: Implement a mandatory roster check-in system to account for every worker at the start, mid-shift, and conclusion of the night shift.

question_text: Supervisors hold current first aid and CPR certification.
recommendation: Enrol supervisors in first aid and CPR certification and keep current cards on file.

question_text: First aid kits are accessible and unobstructed at all times.
recommendation: Relocate first aid kits so they are reachable without a key, a ladder or moving stored material.

question_text: Two-way communication procedures are established between supervisors and crew members.
recommendation: Establish operational two-way communication channels between supervisors and all active field crews.

question_text: Solo workers are equipped with two-way radios or cell phones.
recommendation: Issue functioning two-way radios or mobile phones to any employee working in isolated or remote areas.

question_text: Regular check-in schedules are enforced for isolated workers.
recommendation: Institute mandatory, scheduled periodic check-ins for any personnel working out of sight or earshot.

question_text: Headlight on mobile equipment illuminates the travel path ahead.
recommendation: Equip all mobile equipment with headlights providing minimum 50-foot forward throw illumination in the travel path.

question_text: Mobile equipment is equipped with functional rear-facing lighting.
recommendation: Install operational rear-facing work lights on all mobile equipment operating in the field.

question_text: Overhead and task lighting provides adequate field illumination.
recommendation: Deploy auxiliary floodlight towers or trailer lights to ensure harvesting and walking surfaces are adequately illuminated.

question_text: Working headlamps or hands-free personal lights are issued to all crew members.
recommendation: Issue operational headlamps with spare batteries to all field harvest workers.

question_text: Irrigation canals, ponds, and open water hazards are marked and illuminated.
recommendation: Install reflective markers, physical barriers, and task lighting around all water hazards and canals near active work zones.

question_text: Designated safe muster zones are established for shift start, end, and breaks.
recommendation: Designate and illuminate defined safe staging areas for shift start, ending, and rest breaks away from moving traffic.

question_text: Traffic management plan separates mobile machinery from pedestrian workers.
recommendation: Establish and enforce a field traffic plan that segregates vehicular travel routes from pedestrian harvest crews.

question_text: Workers maintain safe clearance from active tractors, harvesters, and trailers.
recommendation: Enforce minimum safe approach distances between ground workers and active machinery.

question_text: Harvest workers walk within designated row paths and avoid running.
recommendation: Instruct crew members to maintain a steady walking pace and strictly prohibit running between crop rows.

question_text: Workers cross crop rows at designated ends rather than cutting through trellises and wires.
recommendation: Enforce row end crossover routes to eliminate trip exposures from hidden trellis wires, stakes, and irrigation tubing.

question_text: High-visibility reflective vests or apparel are worn by all workers.
recommendation: Require all personnel on the night shift to wear clean, visible retroreflective vests or outer garments.

question_text: Field equipment receives pre-shift mechanical inspections and safety guards are in place.
recommendation: Perform pre-shift safety inspections on all field equipment and replace any missing mechanical guards before use.

question_text: Responsible person is assigned to maintain buildings and grounds
recommendation: Designate a responsible individual to oversee daily grounds maintenance and facility upkeep.

question_text: Site inspection records are documented and retained.
recommendation: Document each site safety inspection with date, findings and corrective actions, and retain the records.

question_text: All safety and maintenance issues from previous inspections are resolved
recommendation: Complete corrective actions for all unresolved items identified on previous inspection logs.

question_text: Living space provides at least 100 square feet per occupant
recommendation: Adjust living quarter occupancy to ensure a minimum of 100 square feet of floor space per resident.

question_text: Housing interior is clean and orderly
recommendation: Thoroughly clean living quarter interiors and establish a regular housekeeping schedule.

question_text: Facilities are free of vermin, vectors, and unsanitary conditions
recommendation: Exterminate pests, seal entry points, and eliminate standing unsanitary matter throughout the premises.

question_text: Abandoned appliances, inoperable vehicles, and derelict equipment are removed
recommendation: Remove all unused appliances, junk, and inoperable equipment from the housing grounds.

question_text: Emergency response plan is posted and available 24 hours daily
recommendation: Post a 24-hour emergency response plan with clear contact instructions in all common areas.

question_text: Housing rules and emergency policies are clearly posted
recommendation: Post housing rules and policy enforcement procedures visibly in all primary occupant languages.

question_text: Exterior unit numbers are clearly posted on each building
recommendation: Install clearly visible numbers on the exterior of all living units for emergency identification.

question_text: Security perimeter fences are intact and maintained
recommendation: Repair damaged sections of security fencing and secure all boundary access gates.

question_text: Doors have functional latching hardware and operational interior locks
recommendation: Install functional latching door handles and operational interior privacy and security locks.

question_text: Outdoor common areas and pathways have adequate illumination
recommendation: Repair non-working outdoor fixtures and provide sufficient lighting along all walkways and gathering areas.

question_text: Living unit structure, walls, floors, and ceilings are in good repair
recommendation: Repair damaged structural surfaces including holes, damaged drywall, and cracked flooring.

question_text: Ceilings maintain an average clearance of at least 7 feet
recommendation: Cease housing occupants in rooms that do not meet the minimum 7-foot ceiling height requirement.

question_text: Windows open smoothly and operate properly
recommendation: Repair or unstick all jammed windows to ensure smooth operation for ventilation and emergency escape.

question_text: Window screens are present, tear-free, and tightly fitted
recommendation: Repair or replace torn, loose, or missing window screening.

question_text: Exterior entrance screen doors are intact and functional
recommendation: Install or repair tight-fitting screen doors on all exterior living unit entrances.

question_text: Separate, sturdy, and comfortable bed is provided for each occupant
recommendation: Provide an elevated, structurally sound bed and clean mattress for every resident.

question_text: Personal storage facilities or lockers are provided for each occupant
recommendation: Provide personal storage lockers or sturdy dressers for occupant belongings in sleeping quarters.

question_text: Dry grass and weeds are cleared away from all buildings
recommendation: Cut back weeds and clear combustible brush to maintain defensible fire clearance around buildings.

question_text: Smoke alarms are installed, functional, and test properly
recommendation: Replace missing batteries and install operational smoke alarms inside each sleeping unit.

question_text: Carbon monoxide detectors are installed and operating properly
recommendation: Install operational carbon monoxide detectors in living quarters adjacent to fossil fuel equipment.

question_text: Living units have a 2A-10BC fire extinguisher within 100 feet
recommendation: Mount charged 2A:10B:C fire extinguishers so travel distance does not exceed 100 feet from any unit.

question_text: Dormitory floor space has at least 2 units of Class A extinguisher rating per 5,000 square feet
recommendation: Install certified Class A fire extinguishers meeting the minimum rating for dormitory square footage.

question_text: Premises are kept free of hazardous combustible waste accumulations
recommendation: Remove hazardous piles of trash, scrap lumber, and combustible debris from around living quarters.

question_text: First aid kits are accessible and unobstructed at all times.
recommendation: Relocate first aid kits so they are reachable without a key, a ladder or moving stored material.

question_text: Supervisors hold current first aid and CPR certification.
recommendation: Enrol supervisors in first aid and CPR certification and keep current cards on file.

question_text: Electrical panels have complete directory labels identifying every breaker
recommendation: Label every circuit breaker clearly in the panel to show the exact room or equipment served.

question_text: Electrical junction boxes, outlets, and switches have secure cover plates
recommendation: Install approved switch, receptacle, and junction box faceplates over all exposed wiring.

question_text: Receptacles and interior light fixtures are operational
recommendation: Replace burned-out bulbs and repair inoperable light switches and wall outlets.

question_text: GFCI receptacles in kitchens, bathrooms, and laundry rooms trip and reset correctly
recommendation: Replace defective GFCI outlets or install GFCI circuit breakers for all wet-area branch circuits.

question_text: Gas-fired heating appliances have an accessible manual shut-off valve
recommendation: Install an accessible manual gas shut-off valve upstream of each heating unit.

question_text: Heating equipment is clean, free of grease, and vented to the outside
recommendation: Clean heating burners, remove grease accumulations, and vent flue gases completely outdoors.

question_text: Solid or liquid fuel radiant heaters maintain at least 36 inches clearance from combustibles
recommendation: Relocate combustible materials to maintain at least 36 inches clearance from radiant heaters.

question_text: Solid or liquid fuel circulating heaters maintain at least 12 inches clearance from combustibles
recommendation: Maintain at least 12 inches of unobstructed space between circulating heaters and combustible walls.

question_text: Gas space heaters maintain at least 6 inches clearance from combustibles
recommendation: Clear all combustibles to provide at least 6 inches of clearance around gas space heaters.

question_text: Heating appliance underside maintains at least 4 inches of open clearance
recommendation: Elevate heating appliances on legs or blocks to provide a minimum 4-inch open air gap underneath.

question_text: Sheet metal floor protection under fuel heaters extends at least 6 inches on sides
recommendation: Install sheet metal extending at least 6 inches beyond the sides and rear of fuel heaters over wood floors.

question_text: Sheet metal under fuel heaters extends at least 18 inches on ash removal sides
recommendation: Extend sheet metal floor protection at least 18 inches in front of heater ash cleanout openings.

question_text: Air conditioning and evaporative coolers are serviced and operating
recommendation: Service cooling equipment, replace dirty air filters, and verify adequate room cooling.

question_text: Potable water supply is continuous, fresh, and abundant
recommendation: Restore an uninterrupted supply of certified potable drinking water for all residential facilities.

question_text: Seasonal water wells are disinfected and chlorinated prior to occupancy
recommendation: Disinfect and shock-chlorinate seasonal private water wells and test water before seasonal opening.

question_text: Water supply lines and waste drains are free of visible leaks
recommendation: Repair leaking supply lines and clear dripping or blocked drain pipes in kitchens and bathrooms.

question_text: Water heaters are operational and supply hot running water
recommendation: Repair or replace defective water heaters to deliver reliable hot water to all living and bathing units.

question_text: Toilets flush and drain properly without back-ups
recommendation: Unclog and rebuild malfunctioning toilets to ensure sanitary waste flushing and drainage.

question_text: Septic systems and waste lines operate without surface overflow
recommendation: Pump and repair failed septic tank drainfields to eliminate exposed sewage effluent.

question_text: Handwashing sinks are located adjacent to toilet facilities
recommendation: Provide handwashing sinks supplied with running water immediately adjacent to all toilet areas.

question_text: Ratio of showers and toilets meets minimum standard of one per 15 occupants
recommendation: Install additional showers and toilets to maintain at least one fixture per 15 residents.

question_text: Bathing facilities are clearly designated by gender signage
recommendation: Post clear gender-designated signs or universal privacy locks on all shower and toilet rooms.

question_text: Shower stalls have functional floor drains and waterproof, nonabsorbent surfaces
recommendation: Resurface damaged shower walls with waterproof material and unclog floor drains.

question_text: Shower light fixtures are enclosed, gasketed, and moisture-proof
recommendation: Install vapor-tight, gasketed moisture-proof light enclosures over shower stalls and bathtubs.

question_text: Clothes washers are functional with plumbed waste drains and dryer vents
recommendation: Plumb clothes washer waste lines to sanitary drains and exhaust dryer ducts directly outside.

question_text: Mess halls and central kitchens have valid local health permits posted
recommendation: Post current local health department operating permits visibly in the dining and food prep area.

question_text: Food service staff hold active food handler certifications
recommendation: Ensure all commercial kitchen food preparation workers obtain valid food handler certification cards.

question_text: Kitchen surfaces and cooking appliances are clean and sanitary
recommendation: Degrease stoves and deep-clean all food prep tables, walls, and floors to sanitary standards.

question_text: Cooking ranges operate properly with all burner valve knobs installed
recommendation: Repair defective stove elements and install control knobs on all burner gas valves.

question_text: Mechanical guards are installed over moving parts on kitchen machinery
recommendation: Reinstall protective interlocks and safety guards over mixers, slicers, and grinder mechanisms.

question_text: Refrigerator temperature maintains 45 degrees Fahrenheit or colder
recommendation: Adjust refrigerator cooling controls or service compressor to maintain food storage at 45°F or below.

question_text: Dining area provides adequate tables, chairs, and dedicated cold storage
recommendation: Provide sufficient dining tables, chairs, and domestic refrigerators inside each residential unit.

question_text: Food supplies are stored elevated off the floor on secure shelving
recommendation: Elevate all bulk dry food boxes on shelving at least 6 inches off the kitchen floor.

question_text: Heavy shelving units are securely anchored to wall studs or floor
recommendation: Anchor tall wire and wooden kitchen shelving units securely to wall framing to prevent tip-overs.

question_text: Waste receptacles are cleanable, fly-tight, and rodent-proof
recommendation: Provide heavy-duty waste containers equipped with tight-fitting pest-resistant lids.

question_text: Kitchens have a Class B-C fire extinguisher rated at least 20 units
recommendation: Mount an approved commercial kitchen fire extinguisher with at least a 20-B:C rating near the cookline.

question_text: Written fleet safety and vehicle maintenance program is implemented
recommendation: Implement a written fleet safety policy establishing mandatory maintenance schedules and driver rules.

question_text: H2A transport drivers are enrolled in the California Employer Pull Notice program
recommendation: Enroll all passenger-transport drivers in the California DMV Employer Pull Notice (EPN) monitoring system.

question_text: Working seat belts are provided and operational for every passenger seat
recommendation: Install and repair functional seat belts for every designated passenger seat in transport vans and buses.

question_text: Trash corral gates remain closed when not actively transferring waste
recommendation: Keep trash corral gates closed and latched when waste transfers are complete.

question_text: Trash compactor operates strictly under key control with a functional dead man switch
recommendation: Repair the dead man switch and implement key control so only trained personnel can operate the compactor.

question_text: Drive-thru lane is adequately illuminated throughout operational hours
recommendation: Repair inoperative light fixtures along the drive-thru lane to provide sufficient illumination.

question_text: Drive-thru lane pavement is free of potholes and tripping hazards
recommendation: Patch broken asphalt and eliminate trip edges in the drive-thru pavement.

question_text: Exterior walkways and entry approaches have intact, level pavement free of trip hazards
recommendation: Repair uneven walkway pavers, cracked concrete, and surface trip hazards along all pedestrian paths.

question_text: Exterior light fixtures are fully illuminated and shielded against breakage
recommendation: Replace burned-out exterior bulbs and install protective shatter-resistant covers on all fixtures.

question_text: Parking lot surfaces are free of potholes, depressions, and curb trip hazards
recommendation: Repair parking lot potholes and clearly paint deteriorated wheel stops and curbs.

question_text: Exterior gas meters and electrical transformers are protected by impact bollards
recommendation: Install steel bollards or guard posts to shield exterior gas meters and transformers from vehicular impact.

question_text: Combustible trash and dumpsters are positioned away from exterior combustible walls
recommendation: Relocate waste dumpsters and combustible refuse containers at least 5 feet away from exterior building walls.

question_text: Exit signs are illuminated and clearly visible from all dining and lobby areas
recommendation: Restore illuminated exit signs to operating condition and replace burned-out backup bulbs.

question_text: Lobby light fixtures are fully operational and shielded against bulb breakage
recommendation: Install shatter-resistant diffusers or covers on all lobby overhead light fixtures.

question_text: Restroom floors are dry, clean, and free of standing water
recommendation: Mop pooled water immediately and repair leaking plumbing fixtures in customer restrooms.

question_text: Biohazard spill cleanup kit stocked with fluid-resistant PPE is available
recommendation: Provide a dedicated bodily fluid spill kit equipped with PPE, absorbent solidifier, and disinfectant.

question_text: Ceiling tiles are intact, clean, and seated securely in their grid
recommendation: Replace stained, sagging, or missing ceiling tiles and align them securely within the grid.

question_text: Entrance and dining doors open and close smoothly without binding
recommendation: Service door hinges and latches so doors open smoothly without excessive resistance or sticking.

question_text: Door closers and hydraulic actuators are free of leaking oil
recommendation: Replace leaking hydraulic overhead door closers and clean fluid residue from door frames.

question_text: Emergency lighting battery units illuminate when tested
recommendation: Service or replace failed emergency lighting batteries to ensure immediate illumination during power loss.

question_text: Wet floor caution signs are available on site
recommendation: Stock at least three functional wet-floor caution signs and place them promptly over spills.

question_text: Floor rugs and runners lie flat and have slip-resistant backing
recommendation: Replace curled or worn floor mats and ensure non-skid rubber backing grips the floor surface.

question_text: Main gas and electrical shutoffs are clearly identified and unobstructed
recommendation: Label main utility shutoff valves and switches clearly and maintain 36 inches of direct clearance.

question_text: Kitchen hood suppression system has been professionally serviced within the past 6 months
recommendation: Schedule a certified service inspection of the automatic hood suppression system and retain current tags.

question_text: Fire extinguisher locations are identified by conspicuous wall signage
recommendation: Mount high-visibility identification signs directly above all fire extinguisher stations.

question_text: Portable fire extinguishers are securely mounted and clear of obstruction
recommendation: Mount portable fire extinguishers on wall brackets between 3 and 5 feet high and remove storage around them.

question_text: Portable fire extinguishers show documented monthly inspection checks on tags
recommendation: Inspect all portable fire extinguishers monthly and initial the inspection tracking tag.

question_text: Class K fire extinguishers are installed in the cooking and frying area
recommendation: Install at least two operable Class K fire extinguishers within 30 feet of commercial fryers and grills.

question_text: Multipurpose ABC fire extinguishers are distributed throughout non-cooking areas
recommendation: Provide at least two operable multipurpose ABC fire extinguishers to cover non-cooking operations.

question_text: Flexible extension cords are not used in place of permanent electrical wiring
recommendation: Remove extension cords powering permanent appliances and have an electrician install hardwired outlets.

question_text: Electrical equipment power cords and plugs are intact and free of damage
recommendation: Take equipment with frayed cords or broken grounding prongs out of service for cord replacement.

question_text: Clearance is maintained below fire sprinkler heads across all areas
recommendation: Reorganize high shelving and remove stock stored within 18 inches of fire sprinkler deflectors.

question_text: Kitchen exhaust hood ductwork and grease baffles are clean and free of heavy grease accumulation
recommendation: Clean grease baffles and contract a certified hood cleaner to remove combustible grease from exhaust ductwork.

question_text: Kitchen floors are degreased, clean, and free of food debris
recommendation: Implement a floor-degreasing schedule to remove slippery oil residues and food debris from line walkways.

question_text: Slip-resistant drainage floor mats are positioned across wet prep and dishwashing stations
recommendation: Place interlocking, slip-resistant drainage mats in all wet ware-washing and food preparation zones.

question_text: Kitchen aisles and prep traffic paths are completely free of obstructions and tripping hazards
recommendation: Clear all crates, trash bins, and prep carts from active kitchen traffic lanes and cookline aisles.

question_text: Energy isolation devices and lockout locks are available for cleaning and servicing machinery
recommendation: Provide designated lockout padlocks and hasps to isolate power sources before cleaning or servicing equipment.

question_text: Floor drain grates are seated flush and free of missing or broken sections
recommendation: Replace broken drain grates and secure them flush with floor surfaces to eliminate tripping hazards.

question_text: Machine guards and safety interlocks are securely installed on food slicers and mixers
recommendation: Reinstall missing blade guards, pusher arms, and interlock cages on commercial food prep equipment.

question_text: Warning signs are posted on high-hazard cutting and mixing machinery
recommendation: Post visible safety warning decals on food slicers, dough mixers, and high-hazard blades.

question_text: Cut-resistant gloves are clean, intact, and accessible near slicing and knife stations
recommendation: Stock cut-resistant mesh or Kevlar gloves and require workers to wear them during knife prep and slicer cleaning.

question_text: Rolling bakery racks and material handling carts have functional, smooth-turning caster wheels
recommendation: Replace seized, broken, or misaligned wheels on rolling bakery pan racks and transport carts.

question_text: Kitchen double-swing doors have unobstructed vision panels
recommendation: Clean view windows on swinging kitchen doors and remove signs or decals blocking opposing traffic visibility.

question_text: Kitchen electrical receptacles near water are GFCI protected and grounded
recommendation: Install and test Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI) receptacles on all kitchen outlets near sinks.

question_text: Rolling dollies are available and used for heavy mop and wash buckets
recommendation: Provide rolling caster dollies for all heavy wash buckets to eliminate manual carrying of liquids.

question_text: Heat-resistant oven mitts, aprons, and thermal arm sleeves are available near cooklines
recommendation: Stock commercial thermal-rated oven mitts and forearm protectors adjacent to ovens, ranges, and broilers.

question_text: Oral medications have been removed from all first aid kits.
recommendation: Remove all oral medications, antiseptics and eye solutions from first aid kits; only a licensed provider may dispense them.

question_text: Small countertop electric appliances are stored securely away from edge fall hazards
recommendation: Position countertop blenders, toasters, and warmers safely back from table edges with cords tucked away.

question_text: Kitchen knives are kept sharp and free of chipped blades
recommendation: Sharpen kitchen cutlery routinely and discard knives with damaged, cracked, or loose handles.

question_text: Kitchen cutlery is stored safely in knife blocks, scabbards, or magnetic strips when not in use
recommendation: Install magnetic wall racks or knife slots and prohibit leaving loose knives in prep sinks and counters.

question_text: Rigid puncture-resistant disposal bins are provided for broken glassware and porcelain
recommendation: Place dedicated rigid plastic or metal disposal containers labeled for broken glass in dishwashing areas.

question_text: Walk-in cooler and freezer floors are level and completely free of ice or frost accumulation
recommendation: Chip away ice build-up, repair leaking evaporator condensation drains, and keep walk-in floors dry.

question_text: Walk-in aisles and interior traffic paths are clear of boxes and milk crates
recommendation: Remove inventory boxes, pallets, and crates from walk-in central aisles to maintain a 36-inch path.

question_text: Walk-in evaporator fan cages and light protective globes are securely in place
recommendation: Reattach safety wire guards over evaporator fans and install vapor-tight globe covers on walk-in lights.

question_text: Walk-in interior light is continuously illuminated or features a luminous internal switch
recommendation: Replace dead walk-in light bulbs and install an illuminated interior toggle switch.

question_text: Walk-in doors have functional interior safety release latches that open without tools
recommendation: Lubricate and service the glow-in-the-dark interior safety door release to prevent personnel entrapment.

question_text: Heavy food stock in walk-in units is stored between knee and chest height
recommendation: Transfer heavy beverage boxes, bulk dressings, and tubs onto middle shelves within the safe lifting zone.

question_text: Stocking hand carts or platform dollies are available for moving heavy cold stock
recommendation: Provide a dedicated two-wheel hand truck or flat platform cart for restocking walk-in storage units.

question_text: Insulated freezer coats and thermal cold-handling gloves are provided for staff entry
recommendation: Hang clean thermal freezer jackets and insulated grip gloves outside the walk-in freezer entrance.

question_text: Clear operational space is maintained around all electrical service panels
recommendation: Clear all boxes and equipment from the 36-inch zone directly in front of and around electrical panels.

question_text: Compressed gas cylinders are chained securely upright and capped when not connected
recommendation: Secure all beverage CO2, helium, and gas cylinders upright with metal chains or rigid brackets.

question_text: Carbon dioxide enrichment or beverage gas systems have operational continuous leak alarms
recommendation: Test the CO2 gas leak detector and recalibrate or replace non-functional sensor alarm units.

question_text: Chemicals and sanitizers are stored in designated areas away from food and packaging
recommendation: Relocate cleaning chemicals, soaps, and sanitizers to separate shelving below and away from food supplies.

question_text: Bulk and heavy inventory boxes are stored within the core lifting zone
recommendation: Reorganize storage racking so heavy containers are placed between knuckle and shoulder height.

question_text: Storage racks and shelving are free of exposed sharp metal edges and pinch points
recommendation: Cover exposed sharp sheet-metal edges on shelving units and remove protruding wire burrs.

question_text: Glass containers and bottled goods are stored at or below eye level
recommendation: Lower glass gallon jugs, glass condiment jars, and bottled beverages to shelves at or below eye level.

question_text: Safety box cutters with auto-retracting blades are provided and used for unboxing
recommendation: Provide spring-loaded self-retracting safety cutters and prohibit the use of exposed fixed utility razors.

question_text: Portable ladders are stored safely on secured wall hooks or chained racks
recommendation: Hang portable step ladders on wall brackets or tie them upright with chains when not in active use.

question_text: Portable ladders are free of structural cracks, bent rungs, and missing slip feet
recommendation: Tag damaged ladders out of service immediately and replace broken rungs or missing non-skid rubber feet.

question_text: Roof access doors and fixed exterior roof ladders remain locked against unauthorized entry
recommendation: Install heavy-duty padlocks on roof hatches and lock security cage gates on exterior roof access ladders.

question_text: Standard 42-inch guardrails or parapets are present along unprotected roof edges
recommendation: Install standard 42-inch perimeter guardrails around roof edge work zones or use certified fall arrest systems.

question_text: Stairs have secure handrails, intact treads, and slip-resistant surface strips
recommendation: Fasten loose stair handrails and replace peeling non-skid safety traction strips on stair treads.

question_text: Commercial laundry washing machines are free of surrounding combustible lint and debris
recommendation: Vacuum dry combustible lint from around commercial washers and clear the utility workspace.

question_text: Damaged or defective equipment is tagged Out of Service and removed from use
recommendation: Affix red Out of Service tags to defective appliances and isolate them from employee use.

question_text: Safety Data Sheets are accessible to employees on every shift.
recommendation: Keep Safety Data Sheets for every hazardous chemical where employees can reach them without asking a supervisor.

question_text: Hazardous chemicals are stored upright in dedicated chemical storage rooms or cabinets
recommendation: Store corrosive and concentrated chemicals upright in a dedicated, ventilated chemical storage locker.

question_text: All secondary chemical containers are labelled with contents and hazards.
recommendation: Label every secondary container with the product name and hazard information before it leaves the storage area.

question_text: Chemical splash goggles, aprons, and neoprene gloves are available at chemical stations
recommendation: Equip chemical dispensing stations with full-seal chemical splash goggles and heavy-duty nitrile gloves.

question_text: First aid kits are accessible and unobstructed at all times.
recommendation: Relocate first aid kits so they are reachable without a key, a ladder or moving stored material.

question_text: Emergency contact numbers and the designated occupational medical clinic are posted
recommendation: Post emergency phone contacts, poison control, and designated medical clinic details next to staff phones.

question_text: All secondary chemical containers are labelled with contents and hazards.
recommendation: Label every secondary container with the product name and hazard information before it leaves the storage area.

question_text: Sources of ignition are kept away from fuel storage and dispensing areas
recommendation: Eliminate all potential ignition sources within the designated fueling and fuel storage perimeter.

question_text: "No Smoking" signs are visibly posted near fuel storage and dispensing areas
recommendation: Post durable "No Smoking" signs prominently around all fuel tanks and refueling locations.

question_text: Dedicated fire extinguishers are available and mounted at fuel storage areas
recommendation: Install and maintain an accessible, properly rated fire extinguisher adjacent to fuel storage.

question_text: Aboveground fuel tanks and valves are structurally sound and in good condition
recommendation: Inspect fuel tanks and repair or replace any corroded, leaking, or damaged components.

question_text: Aboveground fuel storage tanks have secondary containment in place
recommendation: Provide compliant secondary containment basins or dikes capable of holding tank capacity.

question_text: Weeds and combustible vegetation are cleared away from fuel storage areas
recommendation: Clear brush, dry weeds, and combustible vegetation within the fuel tank clearance zone.

question_text: Gas lines and fuel tanks are protected from vehicle impact by bollards
recommendation: Install crash posts, bollards, or wheel stops to protect fuel tanks and piping from vehicle impact.

question_text: Gas lines are equipped with accessible emergency quick-shutoff valves
recommendation: Install accessible emergency quick-shutoff valves on all exposed gas supply lines.

question_text: Clearance from equipment to overhead power lines
recommendation: Maintain a minimum 10-foot clearance between all mobile equipment, booms, and overhead power lines.

question_text: Walkways and work areas have adequate lighting to see hazards clearly
recommendation: Repair or install lighting fixtures to ensure walkways and work areas are adequately illuminated.

question_text: Walkways and common areas are free of trash, scrap piles, and clutter
recommendation: Clear all scrap piles, trash, and loose materials from pedestrian paths and common areas.

question_text: ABC fire extinguishers are mounted and readily accessible in all major buildings
recommendation: Mount fully charged ABC fire extinguishers in conspicuous, unblocked locations across all buildings.

question_text: First aid kits are accessible and unobstructed at all times.
